title: Same bank, opposite reactions: IndusInd’s last two Q1 results show why “good results” can still sink a stock
author: iktisab
selftext:
I pulled daily NSE prices (via Yahoo Finance) around IndusInd Bank’s last two Q1 results:

||Q1 FY26 (Jul 2025)|Q1 FY27 (Jul 2026)|
|:-|:-|:-|
|Net profit YoY|−72%|\+71.7% (₹604 cr → ₹1,037 cr)|
|2 days before results|−5.4%|\+3.5% (Bank Nifty −1.4%)|
|Reaction day close|\+0.8%|−6.0% (Bank Nifty −0.9%)|

Under the FY27 headline, net revenue fell 4.8% (₹6,797 cr → ₹6,471 cr) and fee income fell 17%. The profit rise came mostly from lower costs, on a base hit by the 2025 accounting issue.

My takeaway: the price moved before both announcements, and the reaction followed the surprise, not the headline. It’s one example, not proof, so happy to see counterexamples.
